functions.name: Monitored reset

soft_links.by: door locks released only by the PLC's standstill signal (all axes stopped, 0 V on the actuator bus)
soft_links.why: the PLC is networked: a compromised PLC could release the locks early
soft_links.still: the door switches stay in the hardwired K0 chain: opening a door removes the actuator supply at once

sl.countermeasure: ports locked to the PLC's MAC; nodes in the locked cabinet (physical)
DPI allow-list (C1): only the program's function codes and addresses
SEC-01 read-back, SEC-02 plausibility; TLS on port 802 where offered
not needed at SL 2 for I/O values inside a locked cabinet
the cell switch carries only C1
the firewall's log (SEC-04) to the historian
per-port rate limit; the node watchdog makes loss safe
the PLC checks every HMI write against the tag set and the role
the PLC raises the alarm, the HMI only shows it
the machine runs without the HMI; the panel is replaceable
only the EMS can reach it (C3)
DPI register allow-list: set points only; the reserve is local
the EMS reads back every set point it wrote
not needed at SL 2 for power set points
the EMS alarms on a set point it did not write

attacks.name: rogue coil write
attacks.zone: Z1 (a laptop on the cell switch, or a compromised HMI)
attacks.what: writes HBW Q4 (crane travel) while the Ausleger is out in a slot
attacks.exposure: the Ausleger is out 72.0 s of the 429.8 s order (17 %)
attacks.without: the crane starts sideways at 150 mm/s; the fork (32 mm) has 4 mm each side in the 40 mm shelf gap: it hits the rack after 27 ms
attacks.detect_only: read-back alone (SEC-01) sees it within 40 ms, but by the time the relay drops and the motor coasts to rest the crane has moved 13.5 mm > 4 mm: detection is too late
attacks.with: blocked at conduit C1: the source is not the PLC (port lock + static ARP), so the frame never reaches the node
attacks.residual: a compromised PLC is allowed to write Q4 - only a hardwired interlock stops that (finding F2)

attacks.name: spoofed sensor
attacks.zone: Z1 (man in the middle between the PLC and a node)
attacks.what: answers 'Ausleger back' (HBW I6) while the fork is still in the slot, so the PLC travels
attacks.without: the PLC trusts I6 and travels: the fork is dragged sideways through the shelf (as A1)
attacks.detect_only: the plausibility check catches every early lie: the Ausleger cannot come back in less than 613 ms. A lie sent at that moment is not caught, and the fork is still 23 mm out
attacks.with: C1 locks the cell switch ports to known MACs and pins ARP, so a man in the middle needs the locked cabinet; the plausibility check (SEC-02) catches what physical access might still try early
attacks.residual: authenticated I/O (Modbus/TCP Security, TLS on port 802) on nodes that support it removes the rest

attacks.name: flood a node
attacks.zone: Z1 or anything routed to it
attacks.what: floods the oven node so the PLC's polls time out
attacks.without: SYS-04 after 50 ms, the node's watchdog drops its outputs: safe, but the order loses 33.1 s per event, and an attacker can repeat it
attacks.detect_only: SYS-04 is the detection; it cannot tell a flood from a cable fault
attacks.with: the cell switch rate-limits every port and only the PLC may reach a node; a flood must come from inside the cabinet. SEC-04 names the port
attacks.residual: availability only: the watchdog makes the loss safe (U5 fault F6)

attacks.name: malicious program download
attacks.what: loads a program with the jog interlocks removed
attacks.without: the PLC runs whatever it is given: every software interlock (control.JOG) is gone
attacks.detect_only: a hash compare at the next shift start - after the damage
attacks.with: downloads only via the jump host (C7/C8), with the cabinet key switch in maintenance, and the PLC checks the program against the signed manifest before it leaves INIT (SEC-03)
attacks.residual: the signing key: kept offline, two-person rule

attacks.name: battery reserve drained through the inverter
attacks.what: writes the inverter's minimum reserve to 0 % and forces discharge
attacks.without: the next mains event finds an empty battery: 9 of the month's 10 events relied on it; all 9 would drop the 24 V, costing 60 min of production
attacks.detect_only: the EMS sees the state of charge fall - minutes later; a sag gives no warning
attacks.with: C3's DPI lets the EMS write only the storage set points; the reserve (MinRsvPct) is set on the inverter itself and is not on the allow-list. The inverter's own anti-islanding and export limit stay local (IEEE 1547)
attacks.residual: a compromised EMS can still stop charging: the reserve holds, the bill rises

attacks.name: forged demand-response event
attacks.what: sends a long DR event while the cell produces
attacks.without: U9's EMS covers a DR window from the battery down to its 10 % floor, below the ride-through reserve. At the cell's 86 W peak a window of 2.8 h empties the 200 Wh reserve; the month's longest real event (2.0 h) took 141 Wh and left 59 Wh, against the 55 Wh the longest outage needed. The attacker chooses the length
attacks.detect_only: the event looks like any other
attacks.with: the VEN accepts events only from the pinned VTN certificate (C5), and the EMS will not let a DR event take the battery below the ride-through reserve (a finding for U9: it did)
attacks.residual: a genuine but badly timed event: the EMS opts out when the reserve would be breached

findings.title: Plain Modbus: anything on the cell network could move the machine
findings.text: The nodes cannot authenticate. The allow-list, generated from the program, cuts the 77 mapped signals down to 25 rules; nothing but the PLC may write, and only the coils it drives.

findings.title: F1: 3 outputs were writable that the program never uses
findings.text: vgr.Q7 (compressor); oven.Q10 (compressor); sorting.Q2 (compressor). The compressors Upgrade 1 retired are still wired to live coils. Blocked by the allow-list; the wires should go.

findings.title: F2: detection is too slow for the crane - only prevention works
findings.text: A rogue travel command hits the rack after 27 ms; read-back sees it in 40 ms but the crane has moved 13.5 mm by the time it stops (4 mm clearance). Every jog rule of control.JOG is software: a hardwired contact (Ausleger at its rear stop) in series with the travel relays is the one that matters most.

findings.title: The twin as an intrusion detector: 49 of 49 moving steps
findings.text: A spoofed 'arrived' must still be physically possible. The plant model of Upgrade 5 gives each step a least time; a reply before it is SEC-02. Every step that moves something is covered (7 Upgrade 10 legs move nothing, so a lie there gains nothing). What it cannot catch is a lie told on time over a jammed actuator: a fork reported back at the earliest plausible moment can still be 23 mm out. Authenticated I/O closes that.

findings.title: Safety does not depend on the network - except one soft link
findings.text: No device of the 4 safety functions is networked. The guard locks, though, are released by the PLC's standstill signal: a compromised PLC could unlock early. The door switches still drop K0 the moment a door opens; a standstill monitor on the actuator bus would make the release hardwired too.

findings.title: F3: a forged demand-response event can empty the ride-through reserve
findings.text: U9's EMS covers a DR window from the battery down to its 10 % floor, below the ride-through reserve. At the cell's 86 W peak a window of 2.8 h empties the 200 Wh reserve; the month's longest real event (2.0 h) took 141 Wh and left 59 Wh, against the 55 Wh the longest outage needed. The attacker chooses the length. U9's EMS let a DR window go below the reserve; with U11 it opts out instead.

alarms.text: output read-back differs from the program's image
alarms.cause: a write the program did not make (rogue client, spoofed master) or a node fault
alarms.reaction: every unit holds; the node's outputs are forced off; the firewall log is pulled
alarms.recovery: find the source in the firewall log; acknowledge with the security role

alarms.text: a sensor arrived faster than the plant can move
alarms.cause: a spoofed reply, or a sensor wired wrong
alarms.reaction: the unit goes to FAULT at once, before it acts on the signal
alarms.recovery: inspect the sensor and the node; acknowledge

alarms.text: the running program's hash differs from the signed manifest
alarms.reaction: the PLC does not leave INIT
alarms.recovery: reload the signed program from the engineering station (maintenance mode)

alarms.text: the cell firewall dropped a packet on a conduit
alarms.cause: a device outside its allow-list: scan, misconfiguration or an attack
alarms.reaction: none on the machine: logged and shown

proofs.least_privilege: every read and write of the program allowed; no other coil writable
proofs.default_deny: 20 zone pairs denied; 6 paths from the internet to the cell, each through an authenticated hop
proofs.safety: no networked device in any safety function
proofs.sl: every SL-C gap has a countermeasure
